name: split-focused-devbar-wears-the-ring
description:
A split of two strip tabs, opened by the sidebarTabSplit message a row drop sends (a-row-dropped-on-the-right-edge-opens-a-split drives the real drag). The /note split is no use here: the notes pad is not a strip tab, so no press can make it the active pane.

Every click lands on a point read at run time. AtriumDevBar::PushShadow hands each bar its screen origin as window.atriumDevBarScreenOrigin, because the bar's own window.screenX reads the app window's. The eval adds a point in the bar's page: the centre of the widest bare stretch of the plate, or of the back button, or a spot 150px under the bar for the pane's page, and the click takes that answer through from_eval. The ring is the bar's 'focused' class, which PushDevBarFocusRing sets from the active pane.

Each pane first navigates from a real click on its page, so the entry it leaves keeps a user activation and back is live. A real click on pane 1's bar plate makes pane 1 active. A real click on pane 0's gives the ring back. A click on the url is avoided: it opens the command bar. Then a real click on pane 1's back button takes pane 1 back and leaves pane 0 on its page, and the split stays up.

actions.expression: (() => { const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane) [data-dropzone="tabs"] .tabrow')]; if (rows.length < 2) { return 'rows ' + rows.length; } rows[0].click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: both rows are cold at launch, and a cold row has no tab id

actions.expression: (() => { const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane) [data-dropzone="tabs"] .tabrow')]; if (rows.length < 2) { return 'rows ' + rows.length; } rows[1].click(); return 'clicked'; })()

(() => { const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane) [data-dropzone="tabs"] .tabrow')]; if (rows.length < 2) { return 'rows ' + rows.length; } const dragged = rows[1].dataset.tabId; const target = rows[0].dataset.tabId; if (!dragged || !target) { return 'cold'; } chrome.send('sidebarTabSplit', [dragged, target, 'right']); return 'sent'; })()
actions.note: the message a drop on row 0's right quarter sends

actions.expression: (() => { const p = (() => { const o = window.atriumDevBarScreenOrigin; const bar = document.querySelector('.devbar'); if (!o || !bar) { return 'none'; } const r = bar.getBoundingClientRect(); const y = Math.round((r.top + r.bottom) / 2); let best = [0, 0]; let start = -1; for (let x = Math.ceil(r.left) + 1; x <= Math.floor(r.right); x++) { const bare = x < r.right - 1 && document.elementFromPoint(x, y) === bar; if (bare && start < 0) { start = x; } if (!bare && start >= 0) { if (x - start > best[1] - best[0]) { best = [start, x]; } start = -1; } } if (best[1] - best[0] < 6) { return 'no bare plate'; } return Math.round(o[0] + (best[0] + best[1]) / 2) + ',' + (o[1] + y); })(); return /^[0-9]+,[0-9]+$/.test(p) ? 'ready' : p; })()
